findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-prd.md:AC-6 — AC-6 includes the literal sentence: 'Lane-vs-outcome divergence (e.g. lane assigned Green but blast_radius_outcome = high) is NOT a firing condition — the field's value is recorded for `/insights`-cadence pattern detection.' This sentence verifies a contract about how lane-vs-outcome divergence is recorded for `/insights` consumption, but no R-level requirement in the Requirements section establishes that lane-vs-outcome divergence is captured-and-recorded as a Phase 3 corpus signal. R6 (the elevation rule) explicitly excludes lane-vs-outcome divergence from elevation conditions per interview Round 3's user edit ('drop condition (c) ... a single divergent task isn't a decision; it's a data-point'), but no R says 'the divergence is captured in the entry's `blast_radius_outcome` for `/insights`-cadence consumption.' The AC verifies a contract that no R establishes — the recorded-for-insights claim is in the AC's prose but has no R-level expression. Reverse traceability fails: AC-6's lane-vs-outcome clause is an orphan AC (per goal-driven-reviewer.md anti-pattern: 'An AC that doesn't verify any stated R. Reverse traceability: every AC must trace to ≥1 R').
findings.claim: Coverage gap (orphan AC, reverse traceability failure under E4) — AC-6's lane-vs-outcome-divergence clause verifies a contract about `/insights`-cadence consumption that no R establishes. Goal-Driven Execution principle's reverse traceability: every AC must trace to ≥1 R. The architectural intent (lane-vs-outcome divergence is a corpus signal, not per-task elevation) is correct per interview Round 3's resolution, but the PRD body has no R-level expression of the corpus-signal capture contract. Downstream `specflow:test` building a test plan against this PRD would not have an R to bind the test case to; the test would be testing a sentence in an AC, not a stated requirement.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) add a new requirement that explicitly establishes the corpus-signal capture for lane-vs-outcome divergence: 'R{new}. Lane-vs-outcome divergence captured for `/insights` consumption. The retro entry's `blast_radius_outcome` field (set by `specflow:develop` Phase F.5) and `lane_assigned` field together let `/insights`-cadence pattern detection surface clusters of divergent tasks. The retro skill does not elevate divergence per-task (per R6); the corpus-level signal is downstream. Trace: interview Round 3 (resolution edit) — `lane-vs-outcome divergence is a /insights pattern, not a per-task decision-log entry`. Serves goal: Driving value (corpus-signal preservation for `/insights`-cadence pattern detection).' AND update AC-6 to reference the new R; OR (b) drop the lane-vs-outcome sentence from AC-6 entirely (the AC verifies what the elevation conditions ARE, not what the non-elevation cases produce; the corpus-signal claim doesn't belong in AC-6's scope). Option (a) preserves the architectural intent at R-level expression; option (b) is the surgical edit that removes the orphan claim. Recommend option (a) — the corpus-signal contract is load-bearing for the goal's Driving value (decisions inconsistent failure mode), so it deserves R-level expression.

findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-prd.md:Goal Outcome surface (b) + AC-7 — Goal Outcome surface (b) names: 'when the retro identifies a significant pattern, a corresponding entry appended to `admin/decision-log.md` in the canonical six-field shape.' AC-7 verifies the elevation flow but doesn't verify the SIX-FIELD SHAPE explicitly — AC-7 names five fields (Title, Context, Decision, Rationale, Related) which is correct per `decision-log.md`'s canonical shape (per the example file's preamble: Title / Date / Context / Decision / Rationale / Related — six fields). AC-7's check is on the composed-content shape (5 fields named) but the canonical shape is 6 fields (the Date is missing from AC-7's listed fields). The Date field isn't omitted from the actual write (the skill auto-populates today's date per `specflow:decision`'s convention), but AC-7's verification surface doesn't include it. A retro that wrote a decision-log entry missing the Date field would still pass AC-7 as written.
findings.claim: Soft verification — AC-7 lists five composed fields but the canonical decision-log entry shape is six fields. The verify step misses one of the canonical fields, so a malformed entry (missing Date) would pass the AC. Goal-Driven principle's binary test: 'Could a fresh agent run this step in isolation and tell me unambiguously whether it passed?' A fresh agent reading AC-7 would not know to check for Date because AC-7 doesn't list it.
findings.proposed_change: Edit AC-7 to add Date to the listed composed fields: 'the skill composes the `decision-log.md` entry (Title = `Retro: {task title}`; Date = today; Context = task PRD anchor; Decision = '{user-stated lesson} — pattern surfaced via specflow:complete'; Rationale = the retro field that fired the elevation, quoted; Related = task-history entry id + PRD path).' Six fields total, matching `decision-log.md`'s canonical shape. The verify-step now exercises the full canonical shape; a malformed entry (missing any of the six) would correctly fail.
